stories.title: British watchdog seeks tougher terms around Microsoft's dominance of business software
stories.headline: British watchdog seeks tougher terms around Microsoft's dominance of business software
stories.summary: The UK's competition watchdog wants to designate Microsoft with strategic market status (SMS) in business software, allowing the regulator it to intervene to level the playing field, and says it is considering other areas for investigation. Regulators around the world are watching to see what the UK decides in this case, with bodies such as the US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and the European Commission mulling similar actions. The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) is opening a consultation on whether to tag the Redmond software giant with strategic market status in respect of its portfolio of business software applications.
stories.expanded:
The UK's competition watchdog wants to designate Microsoft with strategic market status (SMS) in business software, allowing the regulator it to intervene to level the playing field, and says it is considering other areas for investigation. Regulators around the world are watching to see what the UK decides in this case, with bodies such as the US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and the European Commission mulling similar actions. The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) is opening a consultation on whether to tag the Redmond software giant with strategic market status in respect of its portfolio of business software applications.

This follows an investigation the regulator started back in May into Microsoft’s software portfolio including Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint and Teams, plus its security, server and operating systems. The watchdog is also probing whether Microsoft enjoys a position of “substantial and entrenched market power” through the suite of software that could be seen as stifling competition and harming buyer choice. It lays out its proposed decision in a document [PDF] and is inviting comments that must be submitted by November 13.

The CMA will make its final decision by February 13, 2027. Bargain spotter The CMA makes it clear the company holds a strong position in each of the five areas it investigated (personal computer operating systems, productivity software suites, security software, server operating systems and relational database management systems), and that customers face barriers when switching providers – limiting their choice and weakening the ability of other software developers to offer rival products. Its proposal document notes Microsoft has been by far the largest provider of business software in the UK for decades.

stories.title: Open source sovereignty gets down to the boring business of making it work
stories.headline: Open source sovereignty gets down to the boring business of making it work
stories.summary: AI and digital sovereignty dominated this year's Open Source Summit Europe. But beyond the AI noise, the sovereignty discussions offered something useful: practical plans for putting open source to work. The recurring theme of digital sovereignty started right from the first day's keynotes, with Geopolitics, Sovereignty, and the Fight to Stay Open, by the Linux Foundation's Nithya Ruff and Johan Linaker from Research Institutes of Sweden, whose name is considerably longer than its URL: ri.
stories.expanded:
AI and digital sovereignty dominated this year's Open Source Summit Europe. But beyond the AI noise, the sovereignty discussions offered something useful: practical plans for putting open source to work. The recurring theme of digital sovereignty started right from the first day's keynotes, with Geopolitics, Sovereignty, and the Fight to Stay Open, by the Linux Foundation's Nithya Ruff and Johan Linaker from Research Institutes of Sweden, whose name is considerably longer than its URL: ri.

This isn't just some European issue. Ruff stressed that it mattered "from Canada, to Sierra Leone, to Trinidad and Tobago. " This was followed by Open Source Security as the Foundation of European Sovereignty, focusing on OSS supply chains.

Then ORBIT Launchpad: Building the Due Diligence Bridge Between Manufacturers and Open Source, with speakers from Dell and Microsoft discussing OpenSSF's efforts to build catalogs of open source components to help companies achieve CRA compliance, such as CRABFOSC – the CRA Baseline For Open Source Consumption. The EU's Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) is now starting to bite: reporting obligations for actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents began last month, with its main requirements applying from December 2027. Hearing Dell and Microsoft discuss how to meet those requirements, rather than simply why they matter, was encouraging.

stories.title: Postgres 19 delayed after AI reviewers find more bugs than humans can fix
stories.headline: Postgres 19 delayed after AI reviewers find more bugs than humans can fix
stories.summary: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group has delayed the release of PostgreSQL 19, the latest iteration of the popular open source database, and held back an unusual number of features. Once slated for release in late September or early October, PostgreSQL 19 is now expected to be generally available around November 19. Developers have also dropped between eight and 10 significant features.
stories.expanded:
The PostgreSQL Global Development Group has delayed the release of PostgreSQL 19, the latest iteration of the popular open source database, and held back an unusual number of features. Once slated for release in late September or early October, PostgreSQL 19 is now expected to be generally available around November 19. Developers have also dropped between eight and 10 significant features.

Explaining the number of reverts — features whose rollouts have now been postponed to next year's release, PostgreSQL 20 — Peter Eisentraut, veep at EDB, a PostgreSQL support and consultancy, said the reason could be at least in part attributed to the LLM code reviews used by developers. In a blog post, Eisentraut, who is a leading PostgreSQL committer, said some of the reverted features had significant architectural defects that would have been hard to fix "quickly and during beta. " However, the introduction of LLM-assisted code review also uncovered a long tail of “relatively harmless issues involving various edge cases” which, in past times, developers might not have noticed until much later, most likely issuing bug fixes in the five years following launch.

“With LLM-assisted code review, these kinds of things can get found much faster, and then you’re staring at a list of forty defect reports. Even if each of them requires only a three-line fix on average, there is a fixed overhead to dealing with each of these, and then you run out of time. ” When the big updates for PostgreSQL 19 were written, LLM-assisted code review was not as useful as it is now, we're told, but in the months leading up to the launch, the AI-supported reviews became better understood and more effective.

stories.title: Want your AI chats to stay private? Brave TEEs up end-to-end encryption
stories.headline: Want your AI chats to stay private? Brave TEEs up end-to-end encryption
stories.summary: Brave Software has set up a secure space so those using its browser can converse with the company's AI assistant in private. At a time when AI agents like Meta's Muse ask for extensive access to personal information, and AI companies repurpose conversations for training, this amounts to swimming against the tide. Following up on an experiment launched last November to implement a confidential channel for LLM conversations with the help of NEAR AI's trusted execution environment (TEE), the browser maker has connected its Leo AI assistant to Z.
stories.expanded:
Brave Software has set up a secure space so those using its browser can converse with the company's AI assistant in private. At a time when AI agents like Meta's Muse ask for extensive access to personal information, and AI companies repurpose conversations for training, this amounts to swimming against the tide. Following up on an experiment launched last November to implement a confidential channel for LLM conversations with the help of NEAR AI's trusted execution environment (TEE), the browser maker has connected its Leo AI assistant to Z.

3 Flash under the protection of end-to-end encryption. The result is that Brave users can submit a prompt to Leo that gets encrypted on-device and sent over the network using Oblivious HTTP, a protocol for separating network requests from associated content. Brave's AI Gateway forwards the encrypted query to the TEE without passing along the user's IP address.

After Brave verifies the enclave's attestation, the browser encrypts the query using a key bound to the TEE. The TEE decrypts the request, runs it through the AI model, and sends back an encrypted response that gets decrypted by the receiving browser. "In 2014, I argued in 'Trust but Verify' that users shouldn't have to place blind trust in the software they rely on," said Brendan Eich, co-founder and CEO of Brave, in a statement.

stories.headline: The Surface Laptop Ultra delivers on most of Microsoft's promises
stories.summary: Over the past week, the laptop Microsoft sent me has been summarizing books and movies, generating images from my imagination, and running a 70-billion-parameter AI model that would be a stretch to fit on most laptops. It also played AAA games at a speed and fidelity I would have thought impossible on an ARM system just a year ago. Microsoft wants to sell you one computer for all of your needs, and for once that doesn't feel like total marketing fluff.

Microsoft wants to sell you one computer for all of your needs, and for once that doesn't feel like total marketing fluff.

Microsoft is throwing both arms around the new Nvidia RTX Spark platform with the Surface Laptop Ultra—and setting its sights on the would-be MacBook Pro buyer, or as the company called it, "a high performance audience. " The bet is that rather than a gaming desktop for fun and a development laptop for work, buyers will pay more for one machine that does both. The Surface Laptop Ultra arrives at a strange time in personal computing.

Recent industry numbers showed a 20 percent drop in total PC shipments year over year in the third quarter of 2026. That's not just consumer purchasing either—that's across the board. Between the RAMpocalypse that has exploded consumer prices and an industry fixated on enterprise money, there hasn't been much new hardware to excite PC enthusiasts.

stories.title: When faster supercomputers aren’t enough
stories.headline: When faster supercomputers aren’t enough
stories.summary: When a million veterans shared their genetic data by enrolling in the Department of Veterans Affairs' “Million Veteran Program,” they expected nothing back. This did not surprise Ravi Madduri, a senior scientist with the Data Science and Learning Division at the U. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory.
stories.expanded:
When a million veterans shared their genetic data by enrolling in the Department of Veterans Affairs' “Million Veteran Program,” they expected nothing back. This did not surprise Ravi Madduri, a senior scientist with the Data Science and Learning Division at the U. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory.

He is abundantly clear about the terms under which these veterans donated their data: “Even after giving everything to the country, they found it in their hearts to give more without expecting anything in return. ” That gift, which constituted the nation’s largest biorepository and most ancestrally varied cohorts of veteran data in the world, created a debt that Madduri, who also holds a joint appointment in the Department of Human Genetics at the University of Chicago, is working to repay. “What I feel when I look at that data is that I have an obligation to deliver to the veterans on their intentions in doing this,” he says.

Those intentions, as he reads it, are that others, veteran or not, can benefit from whatever the data can reveal. “We cannot dilly dally,” Madduri says. After arriving at Argonne as a graduate student in 2001, Madduri has spent the last two decades at the intersection of supercomputing and biomedicine, much of the time building the computing that turns the veterans’ data into results impacting areas from post-traumatic stress disorder to heart disease to cancer.

stories.title: Metropolitan Police's unchecked use of shoplifting platform lands force in trouble with data watchdog
stories.headline: Metropolitan Police's unchecked use of shoplifting platform lands force in trouble with data watchdog
stories.summary: The Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) has reprimanded London's Metropolitan Police Service (MPS) and issued an enforcement notice after officers used a retail crime platform without the force's approval or required data protection checks. Between March 2023 and September 2024, MPS officers registered around 500 free accounts on Auror, a platform retailers use to record crimes such as shoplifting. The force had not formally procured the service or completed the required data protection checks.
stories.expanded:
The Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) has reprimanded London's Metropolitan Police Service (MPS) and issued an enforcement notice after officers used a retail crime platform without the force's approval or required data protection checks. Between March 2023 and September 2024, MPS officers registered around 500 free accounts on Auror, a platform retailers use to record crimes such as shoplifting. The force had not formally procured the service or completed the required data protection checks.

Retailers such as supermarkets encouraged officers to use Auror and directed them to the platform to access CCTV footage. Auror Europe, registered in England and Wales, is a subsidiary of New Zealand-based Auror. The platform allows retailers to share incident reports, images, and CCTV footage.

Retailers pay for access through a browser or mobile app, while police partners use it free of charge. The force had not completed a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) or established data-sharing agreements with Auror Europe, the ICO says. Between August and September 2024, two separate internal security reports were filed regarding officers' use of Auror.

stories.title: KDE hits 30, decides it's time to move out of the X11 era
stories.headline: KDE hits 30, decides it's time to move out of the X11 era
stories.summary: KDE is marking its 30th birthday by showing X11 sessions the door. The newly released KDE Plasma 6. 8 is Wayland-only, though X11 applications can still run through XWayland.
stories.expanded:
KDE is marking its 30th birthday by showing X11 sessions the door. The newly released KDE Plasma 6. 8 is Wayland-only, though X11 applications can still run through XWayland.

The change arrives right on schedule after last month's beta. KWin handles both window management and display-server duties. That means X11-based screen-recording tools, for example, won't work any more.

You can't "shade" windows – roll them up into the title bar and back – and that's not planned to come back. Restoring saved sessions can also behave differently. Applications cannot freely position their own windows under Wayland, leaving placement to the compositor.

But a handful of sites have taken to giving AI agents the finger via HTTP headers, the metadata sent with web page content.

When security biz Signals Corps sampled 217 million HTTP page responses from Common Crawl, it found almost 8,000 sites communicating with AI agents via header messages. Much of this messaging – 7,271 sites – transmitted pointers telling the AI agents where to go next, and 6,989 of the sites sent the x-llms-txt header. stories.headline: Bank of America had to bring in 1,000 contractors to patch all the bugs Mythos identified
stories.summary: Bank of America recruited an additional 1,000 contractors to help patch all the vulnerabilities discovered by Anthropic’s Mythos model, the CEO said on Wednesday. Brian Moynihan, chairman and CEO at BoA, said during the company’s Q3 earnings call that it spent “a couple of hundred million plus” in remediation costs related to Mythos, and the anti-money laundering (AML) orders issued this week. These costs are expected to decline over time, though, with the contractors in place to help ease the initial burden of patching a large number of flaws, an issue that shouldn’t be so pronounced in the longer term.
stories.expanded:
Bank of America recruited an additional 1,000 contractors to help patch all the vulnerabilities discovered by Anthropic’s Mythos model, the CEO said on Wednesday. Brian Moynihan, chairman and CEO at BoA, said during the company’s Q3 earnings call that it spent “a couple of hundred million plus” in remediation costs related to Mythos, and the anti-money laundering (AML) orders issued this week. These costs are expected to decline over time, though, with the contractors in place to help ease the initial burden of patching a large number of flaws, an issue that shouldn’t be so pronounced in the longer term.

He went on to tell CNBC that the bank brought in outside help after concerns grew over how it would quickly tackle all the work associated with Mythos’ discoveries. The same concerns were shared globally, in part due to how Anthropic marketed Mythos as an all-powerful model that threatened the status quo of cybersecurity. While it ultimately turned out to be highly effective and capable of identifying complex vulnerabilities quicker than humans, leading to the massive influx of patches, some early adopters say it was no smarter than elite researchers.

Mozilla CTO Bobby Holley said in April: "So far we've found no category or complexity of vulnerability that humans can find that this model can't," after Mythos found 271 flaws in Firefox 150. "We also haven't seen any bugs that couldn't have been found by an elite human researcher. " The 1,000 contractors brought in by the bank in its Q2 added to its existing 3,000 technical staff.
